myths.fact_zh: 它是活的，只是睡著了。有了水、溫度和空氣，它就能生長。

myths.myth_en: A seed needs sunlight to start growing.
myths.myth_zh: 種子要曬到太陽才會開始長。
myths.fact_en: Many seeds start in the dark, under the soil. The light is needed later, by the leaves.
myths.fact_zh: 很多種子在土裡、在黑暗中就能開始長。光是後來葉子才需要的。

myths.myth_en: You must plant a seed the right way up.
myths.myth_zh: 種子一定要擺正了種。
myths.fact_en: The root finds its way down and the shoot finds its way up, however the seed lies.
myths.fact_zh: 不管種子怎麼躺，根都會自己往下，芽都會自己往上。

myths.myth_en: The more water, the better.
myths.myth_zh: 水愈多愈好。
myths.fact_en: A seed under water gets too little oxygen. It needs damp soil with air in it.
myths.fact_zh: 泡在水裡的種子得不到足夠的氧氣。它需要的是潮溼、而且含有空氣的土。

tricks.body_en: Coat, tiny plant, stored food.
tricks.body_zh: 種皮、小植物、存好的養分。

tricks.body_en: Water, warmth, and air.
tricks.body_zh: 水、溫度和空氣。

tricks.body_en: Gravity tells it which is which.
tricks.body_zh: 重力告訴它哪邊是哪邊。

tricks.body_en: Leaves must open before the lunch is gone.
tricks.body_zh: 便當吃完之前，葉子要展開。

materials.en: A clear jar, paper towels, and water
materials.zh: 一個透明的罐子、幾張紙巾和水

materials.en: Four dried beans, such as mung beans or red beans
materials.zh: 四顆乾豆子，例如綠豆或紅豆

steps.en: Roll the paper towels and line the inside of the jar. Wet them well, and pour away any water that collects at the bottom.
steps.zh: 把紙巾捲起來，貼在罐子的內壁上。把紙巾澆溼，再把積在底部的水倒掉。

steps.en: Push the beans down between the paper and the glass, each one lying a different way: up, down, and sideways.
steps.zh: 把豆子塞進紙巾和玻璃之間，每一顆擺的方向都不一樣：朝上、朝下、橫著放。

steps.en: Keep the paper damp. Draw each bean every day for a week.
steps.zh: 讓紙巾一直保持潮溼。連續一個星期，每天把每一顆豆子畫下來。

steps.en: Which part came out first? Which way did the roots go? Did it matter how the bean was lying?
steps.zh: 最先出來的是哪個部分？根往哪個方向長？豆子怎麼擺有沒有差別？

activities.tip_en: When the roots are a few centimeters long, turn the whole jar on its side and leave it for two more days. Watch what the tips of the roots do. Do not eat the beans from this activity.
activities.tip_zh: 等根長到幾公分長，把整個罐子放倒，再放兩天，看根的尖端會怎麼做。這個活動用過的豆子不要吃。

materials.en: Two small cups with damp cotton or soil, and six mung beans
materials.zh: 兩個小杯子，裝上溼棉花或土，還有六顆綠豆

materials.en: A cardboard box that covers one cup completely
materials.zh: 一個可以把其中一杯完全罩住的紙箱

steps.en: Put three beans in each cup and keep both cups damp.
steps.zh: 每個杯子放三顆豆子，兩杯都保持潮溼。

steps.en: Leave one cup by a bright window. Cover the other with the box.
steps.zh: 一杯放在明亮的窗邊，另一杯用紙箱罩起來。

steps.en: After a week, measure the tallest plant in each cup, and write down the color of its stem and leaves.
steps.zh: 一個星期之後，量一量每一杯裡最高的那一株，並記下莖和葉子的顏色。

steps.en: Which plants are taller? Which look healthier? Are those the same plants?
steps.zh: 哪一杯的植物比較高？哪一杯看起來比較健康？是同一杯嗎？

activities.tip_en: The plants in the dark will probably be taller, and that does not mean they are doing better. Now put them by the window too, and see how many days it takes for them to turn green.
activities.tip_zh: 暗處的植物很可能比較高，但這不代表它們長得比較好。現在把它們也移到窗邊，看看要幾天才會變綠。

sources.en: A seed is a plant structure containing an embryo and stored nutrients in a protective coat; orchid seeds are the smallest, with about one million seeds per gram
sources.zh: 種子是在保護性種皮內含有胚與儲存養分的植物構造；蘭花種子最小，每公克約一百萬顆

sources.en: The most important outside factors for germination are the right temperature, water, oxygen or air, and sometimes light or darkness; the uptake of water swells the seed and breaks the coat; seeds have a temperature range within which they will germinate; oxygen is used in respiration, the seedling's main source of energy until it grows leaves; a seed buried too deeply or in waterlogged soil can be starved of oxygen
sources.zh: 發芽最重要的外在條件是合適的溫度、水、氧氣（空氣），有時還要光或黑暗；吸水使種子膨脹、種皮破裂；種子各有願意發芽的溫度範圍；在長出葉子之前，幼苗主要靠需要氧氣的呼吸作用取得能量；埋得太深或土壤積水的種子會缺氧

sources.en: The radicle, the embryonic root, is the first part of a seedling to emerge from the seed, and it grows downward
sources.zh: 胚根是幼苗最先從種子冒出來的部分，並且往下生長

sources.en: The cotyledons hold the stored food of the seed; as it is used up they may turn green or wither as the first true leaves take over
sources.zh: 子葉儲存種子的養分；養分用完後，子葉可能變綠行光合作用，或在真葉接手後枯萎

sources.en: Seed dormancy prevents seeds from germinating during unsuitable conditions
sources.zh: 種子休眠使種子不會在不適合的環境條件下發芽

sources.en: Charles Darwin was one of the first to document that roots grow toward gravity and stems away from it; a potted plant laid on its side turns its growing stem upward; dense starch-filled statoliths in the root cap are one way plants sense gravity
sources.zh: 達爾文是最早以科學方式記錄「根向地、莖背地」的人之一；橫放的盆栽，莖的生長部位會轉向上方；根冠裡沉降的澱粉體（平衡石）是植物感知重力的方式之一

sources.en: Seedlings grown without light have long, weak stems and a pale yellow color and lack chlorophyll; this raises the chance of reaching a light source from under the soil
sources.zh: 在無光下生長的幼苗莖細長、顏色淡黃、缺少葉綠素（黃化）；這能提高從土裡伸到有光處的機會

sources.en: Mung bean sprouts are grown by watering sprouted beans in the shade until the stems grow long
sources.zh: 綠豆芽的種法：把發芽的綠豆放在遮蔭處持續澆水，直到下胚軸伸長

sources.en: Date palm seeds found in a jar at Masada in 1963–1965 were radiocarbon dated to between 155 BC and 64 CE; one was sprouted in 2005 and the palm was named Methuselah
sources.zh: 1963–1965 年在馬薩達一個罐子裡發現的椰棗種子，碳十四定年為西元前 155 年到西元 64 年之間；2005 年其中一顆成功發芽，取名瑪土撒拉

sources.en: A 1,300-year-old sacred lotus seed recovered from a dry lake bed in northeastern China was grown in 1995
sources.zh: 中國東北乾涸湖床出土、約 1,300 年的古蓮子，於 1995 年的研究中成功發芽

sources.en: The National Plant Genetic Resources Center began operating in October 1993; by the end of 2005 it held 68,211 accessions; seeds are dried, sealed, and stored cold and dry, with the long-term store at −12 °C
sources.zh: 國家作物種原中心於民國 82 年 10 月開始營運；94 年底保存作物種原 68,211 份；種子乾燥後密封，在低溫低濕下存放，長期庫為 −12 ℃
sources.src: 農業部〈國家作物種原中心及水稻功能基因研究種原之保存〉（農業試驗所） Ministry of Agriculture, Taiwan

lessons.title: Why Do Flowers Bloom?
lessons.blurb_en: Flowers are not there to look pretty for us. They are how a plant makes seeds, and a plant cannot walk over to another plant. In a 3D model, cut a flower open and follow one grain of pollen: carried in by a bee, caught by the stigma, and then growing a tube down to a waiting seed-to-be. Switch to the wind and see why some plants must throw away so much pollen. Last, look at a flower and work out who delivers for it.
lessons.blurb_zh: 花不是為了讓我們覺得好看才開的。花是植物製造種子的方法，而植物沒辦法走到另一株植物那裡去。在 3D 模型裡把一朵花切開，跟著一粒花粉走：被蜜蜂帶進來、被柱頭接住，然後長出一條管子，通到等在那裡的「未來的種子」。換成風來送，看看為什麼有些植物非得浪費那麼多花粉不可。最後看著一朵花，推理出是誰在替它送貨。
lessons.big_idea_en: A flower is the part of a plant that makes seeds. To make a seed, pollen from one flower has to reach the stigma of another. A plant cannot move, so it uses a carrier. Many plants hire animals, and they pay with nectar and advertise with color and scent. Others let the wind do it and make huge amounts of pollen. When pollen arrives, it grows a tube down to an ovule. The ovule becomes a seed, and the part around it becomes a fruit.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 花是植物用來製造種子的部分。要做出種子，一朵花的花粉必須送到另一朵花的柱頭上。植物不能移動，所以要找人送貨。很多植物雇用動物，用花蜜付工錢，用顏色和香味打廣告；另外一些讓風來送，於是得製造非常大量的花粉。花粉送到以後，會長出一條管子通到胚珠。胚珠變成種子，包著它的部分變成果實。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. The flower has been cut open so that you can see inside. Press Pause and move the slider slowly through the four steps. Watch where the pollen lands, and where the orange tube goes. Then choose By wind and run it again. What has changed about the flower, and how much of the pollen arrives?
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。這朵花被切開了，讓你看得到裡面。按「暫停」，慢慢拉動滑桿，走過四個階段。注意花粉落在哪裡、橘色的管子通到哪裡。接著選「風送」再跑一次：這朵花有什麼地方不一樣了？花粉又有多少送得到？

b_carry.en: A bee is coming for the nectar, the sweet drink at the bottom of the flower. The bright petals showed it where to land. It has just been to another flower of the same kind, and that flower's pollen is stuck to its body.
b_carry.zh: 一隻蜜蜂為了花蜜而來——花朵底部那種甜甜的飲料。鮮豔的花瓣告訴牠該降落在哪裡。牠剛剛去過另一朵同一種的花，那朵花的花粉還黏在牠身上。

b_land.en: As the bee pushes in, it brushes against the stigma, the sticky tip in the middle, and leaves pollen there. It also picks up fresh pollen from the anthers to carry to the next flower. The bee gets a meal, and the plant gets a delivery.
b_land.zh: 蜜蜂往裡面鑽的時候，擦過了正中央那個黏黏的頂端——柱頭，把花粉留在上面。同時牠又從花藥沾了新的花粉，帶去下一朵花。蜜蜂吃到一餐，植物的貨也送到了。

w_carry.en: This flower has no bright petals, no scent, and almost no nectar. It does not need them, because the wind does not have to be paid. But the wind does not aim either. The plant lets go of a great cloud of light, dry pollen, and nearly all of it is lost.
w_carry.zh: 這朵花沒有鮮豔的花瓣、沒有香味，也幾乎沒有花蜜。它用不著這些，因為風不必付工錢。可是風也不會瞄準。植物放出一大片又輕又乾的花粉，其中幾乎全部都白白飄走了。

w_land.en: One grain has been caught. Look at the stigma of this flower. It is large and feathery, like a net held up in the air. In the model, one grain in forty arrives. For real plants the chance is far smaller.
w_land.zh: 有一粒被接住了。看看這朵花的柱頭：又大、又像羽毛，就像舉在空中的一張網。在模型裡，四十粒當中到了一粒；真的植物，機會還要小得多。

tube.en: The pollen grain is on the stigma, but the ovules are far below. So the grain grows a thin tube down through the middle of the flower. The tube carries what the ovule is waiting for.
tube.zh: 花粉粒到了柱頭，可是胚珠還在下面很遠的地方。於是花粉粒長出一條細細的管子，穿過花的正中央往下走。管子帶著胚珠在等的東西。

seed.en: The tube has reached an ovule, and the ovule is turning into a seed. Now the flower's work is done. The petals fall, and the ovary around the seed swells into a fruit. The other ovules got no pollen, so they will not become seeds.
seed.zh: 管子通到了一顆胚珠，那顆胚珠正在變成種子。花的工作到這裡就完成了：花瓣掉落，包著種子的子房膨大成為果實。另外幾顆胚珠沒有等到花粉，就不會變成種子。

legend.en: Pink: petals, the signboard
legend.zh: 粉紅色：花瓣，招牌

legend.en: Yellow: anthers and pollen
legend.zh: 黃色：花藥和花粉

legend.en: Green: the stigma, the style below it, and the ovary
legend.zh: 綠色：柱頭、下面的花柱，還有子房

legend.en: Orange line: the pollen tube
legend.zh: 橘色的線：花粉管

legend.en: Orange: the ovary swelling into a fruit
legend.zh: 橘色：子房膨大成果實

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The parts are not to scale: pollen grains are far too small to see like this. The numbers of grains are examples. Real flowers come in thousands of shapes, and many have their parts in different numbers and places. A real wind-pollinated flower usually looks quite different from the other kind, and the model changes only a few things so that you can compare them. The steps shown take hours or days.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型。各部分沒有照比例：花粉粒其實小到不可能這樣看見。花粉的粒數是示意。真的花有成千上萬種形狀，很多花各部分的數目和位置都不一樣。真正靠風傳粉的花，樣子通常和另一類差很多；模型只改了幾個地方，方便你比較。畫面裡的過程，實際上要花幾小時到幾天。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow the sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依本頁最下方列出的出處。

paras: A plant has a problem that an animal does not have. To make seeds, it usually needs something from another plant of its own kind. But it is rooted to the ground and cannot go and get it. A flower is the answer to that problem.

Look into the middle of a flower. Around the center there is a ring of thin stalks, each with a small bag on top. The bags are called anthers, and they make pollen, a fine yellow dust. Right in the center stands the stigma. It is often sticky, and below it, at the bottom of the flower, are the ovules. Each ovule can become a seed.

A seed begins when pollen from one flower lands on the stigma of another. Something has to carry it there. About four out of five kinds of flowering plants use animals: bees, butterflies, moths, flies, beetles, birds, and bats. The animal comes for nectar, a sugary drink, and carries pollen away on its body without meaning to.

This is why so many flowers are bright and sweet-smelling. The color and the scent are advertising, and the nectar is the pay. Some flowers even have lines on their petals that point the way to the nectar.

Other plants use the wind. Grasses and oak trees are like this. Their flowers are small and dull, with no scent, because the wind does not need to be invited. But the wind does not aim, so these plants make enormous amounts of light pollen, and they catch it with stigmas shaped like feathers.

When a grain of pollen lands on the right stigma, it grows a thin tube down to an ovule. Then the ovule becomes a seed, and the part of the flower around it, the ovary, grows into a fruit. A tomato, a peach, and a bean pod were all once the middle of a flower.
paras_zh: 植物有一個動物沒有的難題。要做出種子，它通常需要另一株同類植物身上的東西；可是它的根扎在地上，沒辦法自己過去拿。花，就是用來解決這個難題的。
往一朵花的中間看。圍著中心有一圈細細的柄，每一根的頂端有一個小袋子。這些小袋子叫做花藥，會製造花粉——一種細細的黃色粉末。正中央立著的是柱頭，通常黏黏的；在它的下方、花的最底部，是胚珠。每一顆胚珠都可能變成一粒種子。
一朵花的花粉落到另一朵花的柱頭上，種子才會開始形成。花粉得有人送過去。每五種開花植物裡，大約有四種靠動物：蜜蜂、蝴蝶、蛾、蠅、甲蟲、鳥，還有蝙蝠。動物是為了花蜜（一種含糖的飲料）而來，花粉沾在身上，就這樣在不知不覺中被帶走了。
所以才有這麼多花又鮮豔又香。顏色和香味是廣告，花蜜是工錢。有些花的花瓣上甚至有線條，指出花蜜在哪裡。
另外一些植物靠風。禾草和橡樹就是這樣。它們的花又小又不起眼，也沒有香味，因為風用不著邀請。可是風不會瞄準，所以這些植物會製造非常大量、非常輕的花粉，再用羽毛形狀的柱頭去接。
一粒花粉落在對的柱頭上以後，會長出一條細細的管子，通到一顆胚珠。接著胚珠變成種子，而花朵裡包著它的那個部分——子房——長成果實。番茄、桃子和豆莢，原本都是一朵花的中心。
questions: What problem does a flower solve for a plant?
Why are many flowers bright and sweet-smelling?
What does the ovary of a flower become?
answers: A plant cannot move, so it cannot go to another plant to get pollen. A flower lets something else carry the pollen.
The color and the scent are advertising for animals, and the nectar is their pay for carrying pollen.
It becomes a fruit, with the seeds inside it.

parts.text_en: Watch the bee arrive with pollen on its body, touch the stigma, and leave.
parts.text_zh: 看蜜蜂帶著一身花粉飛來，碰到柱頭，再飛走。

parts.text_en: Forty grains blow past. Count how many of them touch the stigma.
parts.text_zh: 四十粒花粉飄過去。數數看有幾粒碰到柱頭。

parts.text_en: Follow the orange line down from the stigma. Where is it heading?
parts.text_zh: 順著橘色的線從柱頭往下看。它要去哪裡？

parts.text_en: The petals are gone and the ovary has swollen. Find the one ovule that became a seed.
parts.text_zh: 花瓣掉了，子房脹大了。找出變成種子的那一顆胚珠。

lessons.parts_note_en: In both versions, steps 3 and 4 are exactly the same. Only the delivery is different. One plant pays for a careful carrier, and the other pays nothing and sends far more.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 兩種版本的第三、第四階段完全一樣，不一樣的只有送貨的方式：一種植物付錢請仔細的送貨員，另一種一毛錢也不付，但是送出去的多得多。

guesser.lead_en: You can often tell who carries a flower's pollen just by looking at it. Tick what the flower has, and see what that suggests.
guesser.lead_zh: 只要看一朵花的樣子，常常就猜得出是誰替它送花粉。把這朵花有的特徵打勾，看看這代表什麼。

animal.note_en: Bright petals and a sweet smell are advertising, and nectar is pay. A flower spends on these only when it has visitors to attract.
animal.note_zh: 鮮豔的花瓣和香味是廣告，花蜜是工錢。有訪客要吸引，花才會把力氣花在這些上面。

wind.note_en: No show, no scent, and a great deal of light pollen. Grasses and many trees flower like this, and most people never notice.
wind.note_zh: 不起眼、沒有香味，卻有一大堆很輕的花粉。禾草和很多樹就是這樣開花的，大多數人從來沒有注意到。

mixed.note_en: This flower has signs of both. Some plants really do use animals and the wind together, but it is not the usual pattern.
mixed.note_zh: 這朵花兩邊的特徵都有。確實有些植物同時靠動物和風，不過這不是常見的情形。

none.note_en: Tick at least one thing. A flower with nothing to attract a visitor and little pollen to spare may pollinate itself.
none.note_zh: 至少勾一項吧。一朵既沒有東西吸引訪客、花粉又不多的花，也許是自己替自己授粉的。

guesser.note_en: This is a rule of thumb, and flowers are full of exceptions. It works best as a first guess, which you then check by watching the flower.
guesser.note_zh: 這只是一個粗略的判斷方法，花的世界到處都是例外。最好把它當成第一個猜測，再去觀察那朵花來驗證。

facts.eyebrow: Flowers by the Numbers · 花的數字
facts.lead_en: Who carries the pollen, and how far it has to go.
facts.lead_zh: 誰在送花粉，花粉又要走多遠。

items.en: About this share rely on living carriers, mostly insects, to move their pollen.
items.zh: 大約這麼高的比例，是靠生物（大多是昆蟲）來搬運花粉的。

items.en: A typical flower is built in four rings: sepals, petals, stamens, and the pistil in the middle.
items.zh: 典型的花由四圈構成：萼片、花瓣、雄蕊，還有正中央的雌蕊。

items.en: In corn, a single pollen tube can grow longer than this to reach its ovule.
items.zh: 玉米的一條花粉管可以長得比這還長，才到得了胚珠。

items.en: Christian Konrad Sprengel published the idea that flowers exist to attract insects.
items.zh: 施普倫格爾發表了他的看法：花的存在是為了吸引昆蟲。

items.en: Wind-pollinated flowers make little or no nectar and no scent. The wind works for free.
items.zh: 靠風傳粉的花幾乎不製造花蜜，也沒有香味。風是免費的。

items.en: A fruit is the ovary of a flower, grown large after the flower has finished.
items.zh: 果實就是花的子房，在花謝了以後長大而成。

culture_cards.title_en: A teacher nobody believed, hidden lines, the food on your plate, and lights in the fields of Tianwei
culture_cards.title_zh: 沒有人相信的老師、看不見的線條、你盤子裡的食物，還有田尾田裡的燈
culture_cards.lead_en: What people have learned by watching flowers closely.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 人們仔細觀察花朵之後學到的事。

cards.body_en: Christian Konrad Sprengel was a German teacher who spent years watching insects visit flowers. In 1793 he published a book explaining that the purpose of a flower is to attract insects, and that nature favors pollen brought from another plant. Few people took notice. His work was not widely recognized until Charles Darwin tested and confirmed his observations many years later.
cards.body_zh: 施普倫格爾是一位德國教師，花了好多年觀察昆蟲造訪花朵。1793 年他出版了一本書，說明花的功用是吸引昆蟲，而且大自然偏好從別株帶來的花粉。當時沒有什麼人注意。直到很多年以後，達爾文檢驗並證實了他的觀察，他的研究才被廣泛認可。

cards.body_en: Some flowers have marks on their petals that guide a visitor to the nectar, like lines painted on a runway. In some plants, such as the meadow buttercup, the marks show up only in ultraviolet light, which human eyes cannot see. To us the flower is plain yellow. Seen in ultraviolet, it has a dark center where the nectar is.
cards.body_zh: 有些花的花瓣上有記號，把訪客引到花蜜那裡，就像畫在跑道上的線。有些植物（例如草地毛茛）的記號只有在紫外光下才看得出來，而人的眼睛看不見紫外光。在我們眼裡，那朵花是一片單純的黃色；在紫外光下，它的中心是深色的，花蜜就在那裡。

cards.body_en: To a cook, a fruit is something sweet. To a botanist, a fruit is whatever grows from the ovary of a flower and holds the seeds. By that meaning, bean pods and nuts are fruits as well. Next time you cut one open, look for the seeds, and remember that each one began with a grain of pollen.
cards.body_zh: 對廚師來說，水果是甜的東西。對植物學家來說，凡是由花的子房長成、裡面裝著種子的，都是果實。照這個意思，豆莢和堅果也是果實。下次切開它們的時候，找找裡面的種子，並且記得：每一粒種子，最初都是從一粒花粉開始的。

cards.en: Why the fields of Tianwei are lit at night
cards.zh: 田尾的田為什麼晚上點燈
cards.body_en: Chrysanthemums bloom in autumn, when the nights grow long. The plant measures the length of the night, and a long night is its signal to make flower buds. Growers in Tianwei, Changhua, hang lamps over their fields and switch them on after dark. The night is made short, so the plants keep growing and do not bloom. When the growers want flowers, they turn off the lamps. That is how flowers can be ready for the right day, on long stems.
cards.body_zh: 菊花在秋天開花，那時候夜晚變長了。菊花會測量夜晚的長度，夜一長，就是它長出花苞的信號。彰化田尾的花農在田裡吊起燈泡，天黑之後點亮，把長夜變成短夜，菊花就繼續長高而不開花。等到想要花的時候，再把燈關掉。這樣花就能在需要的日子開，而且花莖夠長。

myths.myth_en: Flowers are there to look pretty.
myths.myth_zh: 花是為了好看才開的。
myths.fact_en: Flowers are there to make seeds. The color is advertising for the animals that carry pollen.
myths.fact_zh: 花是為了製造種子。顏色是給搬運花粉的動物看的廣告。

myths.myth_en: Bees visit flowers to help the plant.
myths.myth_zh: 蜜蜂去採花是為了幫植物的忙。
myths.fact_en: Bees come for nectar and pollen to eat. Carrying pollen between flowers is a side effect.
myths.fact_zh: 蜜蜂是為了吃花蜜和花粉而來。在花與花之間搬運花粉，只是順帶發生的事。

myths.myth_en: Grass and trees like oaks have no flowers.
myths.myth_zh: 草和橡樹這類的樹不會開花。
myths.fact_en: They do. Their flowers are small and plain because the wind carries their pollen.
myths.fact_zh: 它們會開花，只是花又小又樸素，因為它們的花粉是風送的。

myths.myth_en: Fruits and flowers are separate things.
myths.myth_zh: 果實和花是兩回事。
myths.fact_en: A fruit grows from the ovary of a flower. Every fruit was once part of a flower.
myths.fact_zh: 果實是由花的子房長成的。每一顆果實，都曾經是花的一部分。

tricks.body_en: That is its whole job.
tricks.body_zh: 這就是它全部的工作。

tricks.body_en: From an anther to another flower's stigma.
tricks.body_zh: 從花藥到另一朵花的柱頭。

tricks.title_en: Pay an animal, or use the wind
tricks.body_en: Nectar and color, or clouds of pollen.
tricks.body_zh: 花蜜和顏色，或是一大片花粉。

tricks.title_en: Ovule to seed, ovary to fruit
tricks.title_zh: 胚珠變種子，子房變果實
tricks.body_en: After a pollen tube arrives.
tricks.body_zh: 在花粉管抵達之後。

safety_head.eyebrow: An Observer's Code · 觀察守則

safety.en: Pick only flowers that you have permission to pick, and never pick wild flowers in a park or a nature reserve.
safety.zh: 只摘得到允許的花；公園和保護區裡的野花不要摘。

safety.en: Watch bees and wasps from an arm's length away, and do not wave at them or try to touch them.
safety.zh: 觀察蜜蜂和胡蜂時，保持一隻手臂的距離，不要揮趕，也不要去碰。

safety.en: Leave every insect where you found it.
safety.zh: 每一隻昆蟲都留在原來的地方。

materials.en: One large flower that you are allowed to pick, such as a lily or a hibiscus
materials.zh: 一朵得到允許可以摘的大花，例如百合或朱槿

materials.en: A sheet of white paper, tape, and a magnifying glass
materials.zh: 一張白紙、膠帶和一支放大鏡

steps.en: Starting from the outside, gently pull off each ring of parts and tape it to the paper in a row.
steps.zh: 從最外面開始，輕輕把每一圈的構造摘下來，在紙上貼成一排。

steps.en: Label each row: sepals, petals, stamens, and the pistil in the middle.
steps.zh: 替每一排寫上名稱：萼片、花瓣、雄蕊，還有正中央的雌蕊。

steps.en: Touch an anther to the paper. Look at the dust it leaves through the magnifying glass.
steps.zh: 拿一個花藥在紙上輕輕碰一下，用放大鏡看它留下的粉末。

steps.en: Ask an adult to cut the bottom of the pistil across. Can you see the ovules inside?
steps.zh: 請大人把雌蕊的底部橫切開來。你看得到裡面的胚珠嗎？

activities.tip_en: Lily pollen stains cloth, so cover the table. Count the parts in each ring. In many flowers the numbers are related, such as three and six, or five and ten.
activities.tip_zh: 百合的花粉會把布染色，桌面先鋪一層紙。數一數每一圈有幾個；很多花各圈的數目是有關係的，例如三和六，或是五和十。

activities.title_zh: 在一朵花旁邊待十分鐘

materials.en: A notebook and a pencil
materials.zh: 一本筆記本和一支鉛筆

materials.en: A patch of flowers outdoors on a warm, dry day
materials.zh: 晴朗溫暖的日子裡，戶外的一小片花

steps.en: Choose one flower, or one small group of flowers, and sit where you can see it clearly.
steps.zh: 選一朵花，或一小叢花，坐在看得清楚的地方。

steps.en: For ten minutes, make a mark for every visitor: bee, butterfly, fly, beetle, or something else.
steps.zh: 在十分鐘裡，每來一位訪客就畫一個記號：蜜蜂、蝴蝶、蠅、甲蟲，或是別的。

steps.en: For each visitor, notice where it lands and which parts of the flower it touches.
steps.zh: 留意每一位訪客降落在哪裡、碰到了花的哪些部分。

steps.en: Do the same at a different kind of flower. Are the visitors the same?
steps.zh: 換一種花再做一次。來的訪客一樣嗎？

activities.tip_en: Try it at different times of day. Some flowers open only in the morning, and some are visited mostly at dusk.
activities.tip_zh: 在一天裡不同的時間試試看。有些花只在早上開，有些花的訪客大多在黃昏才來。

sources.en: Flowers are the reproductive structures of flowering plants, typically built in four rings: sepals, petals, stamens, and the pistil; the stamens present the pollen and the stigma receives it and directs it to the ovules in the ovary; nectar guides may be visible only under ultraviolet light; after pollination and fertilization the resulting cell grows into a seed
sources.zh: 花是開花植物的生殖構造，典型由四輪構成：萼片、花瓣、雄蕊、雌蕊；雄蕊提供花粉，柱頭接收花粉並導向子房內的胚珠；蜜源標記可能只在紫外光下可見；授粉與受精之後發育成種子

sources.en: About 80% of flowering plants rely on biotic pollination; abiotic pollination relies on wind or water; cross-pollination is the delivery of pollen from the stamen of one flower to the stigma of a flower on another plant of the same species
sources.zh: 約 80% 的被子植物仰賴生物傳粉；非生物傳粉靠風或水；異花授粉是花粉由一朵花的雄蕊送到同種另一株植物的花的柱頭

sources.en: Pollinators include bees, wasps, flies, butterflies, moths, and beetles, and among vertebrates mainly bats and birds
sources.zh: 傳粉者包括蜂類、蠅類、蝴蝶、蛾、甲蟲；脊椎動物主要是蝙蝠和鳥類

sources.en: Nectar is a sugar-rich liquid produced by plants, with which flowers attract pollinating animals
sources.zh: 花蜜是植物分泌的含糖液體，花朵用它吸引傳粉的動物

sources.en: Nectar guides are markings that guide pollinators to their rewards; in some plants, such as the meadow buttercup, they are visible only in ultraviolet light, where the flowers have a darker center
sources.zh: 蜜源標記是引導傳粉者找到報酬的花紋；有些植物（如草地毛茛）的標記只在紫外光下可見，花心顏色較深

sources.en: Wind-pollinated flowers lack scent and showy parts, make little nectar, and produce enormous numbers of light, smooth pollen grains; they have large, feathery stigmas; grasses and oaks are wind-pollinated
sources.zh: 風媒花沒有香味、沒有顯眼的構造、花蜜少，製造極大量又輕又光滑的花粉，柱頭大而呈羽毛狀；禾草與橡樹是風媒植物

sources.en: The pollen tube carries the male cells from the pollen grain on the stigma to the ovules; in maize a single tube can grow longer than 12 inches (30 cm)
sources.zh: 花粉管把雄性細胞從柱頭上的花粉粒送到胚珠；玉米的單一花粉管可以長到超過 30 公分

sources.en: In botany a fruit is the seed-bearing structure formed from the ovary after flowering; the term includes nuts and bean pods
sources.zh: 植物學上，果實是開花後由子房形成、內含種子的構造；堅果與豆莢也算果實

sources.en: Sprengel's book of 1793; he was the first to recognize that the function of flowers was to attract insects and that nature favored cross-pollination; his work was not widely recognized until Charles Darwin confirmed several of his observations
sources.zh: 施普倫格爾 1793 年的著作；他最早認識到花的功能是吸引昆蟲、自然界偏好異花授粉；直到達爾文證實他的多項觀察後才受到廣泛認可

sources.en: The chrysanthemum is a short-day plant, in fact a long-night plant, which forms flower buds when the nights grow long; lamps lit at night turn the long night into a short one and hold back flowering, to adjust the harvest date and to lengthen the stems
sources.zh: 菊花是短日植物（其實是「長夜植物」），夜變長時才花芽分化；夜間點燈把長夜變成短夜，抑制開花，用來調節產期並延長花莖
sources.src: 農業部 農業知識入口網 菊花主題館〈菊花為什麼要電照？〉（許謙信撰） Ministry of Agriculture, Taiwan

sources.en: The sea of lights over the chrysanthemum fields is a feature of Tianwei
sources.zh: 「電照菊花的燈海」是田尾的一大特色
sources.src: 彰化縣田尾鄉公所〈電照菊花栽培〉 Tianwei Township Office, Changhua County

lessons.title: How Does Water Reach the Top of a Tree?
lessons.blurb_en: A tall tree lifts water higher than a ten-story building, every day, without a pump and without a heart. In a 3D model, watch a thread of water run from the roots to the leaves, and find out what is doing the lifting. Turn off the sun, dry out the soil, or fill the air with mist, and see the flow slow down or stop. Last, compare some real trees with the highest that sucking alone can ever raise water.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一棵大樹每天都把水送到比十層樓還高的地方，沒有幫浦，也沒有心臟。在 3D 模型裡，看一條水柱從根一路通到葉子，找出到底是誰在出力。把太陽關掉、讓土乾掉，或是讓空氣充滿水氣，看水流怎麼變慢、甚至停下來。最後拿幾棵真的樹，和「只靠吸」最多能把水抬到的高度比一比。
lessons.big_idea_en: A tree has no heart to push water up. The water is pulled up from the top. Water evaporates out of the leaves through tiny pores, and each bit that leaves pulls the next bit up behind it, because water clings to itself. The pull reaches all the way down the trunk to the roots, through very narrow tubes. The sunnier and drier the day, the harder the leaves pull.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 樹沒有心臟可以把水往上推。水是從上面被拉上去的。水從葉子上很小的孔蒸發出去，每離開一點，就把後面的那一點往上拉，因為水會緊緊黏住自己。這股拉力沿著樹幹一路傳到根，走的是非常細的管子。天氣愈晴朗、愈乾燥，葉子拉得就愈用力。

tricks_head.zh: 一句話記住水怎麼往上

lab.how_en: Drag to turn the model, and scroll or pinch to zoom. The blue beads are water, and you can see through the trunk. First watch where the water goes when it reaches the leaves. Then slide Sunlight down to zero. What happens to the beads? Bring the sun back, and try very damp air, and then very dry soil. Each one slows the water for a different reason.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉模型，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。藍色的珠子是水，樹幹畫成透明的，讓你看得到裡面。先看水到了葉子之後去了哪裡。接著把「陽光」拉到零，珠子怎麼了？把太陽加回來，再試試很潮溼的空氣，然後是很乾的土。每一種都會讓水慢下來，但是原因各不相同。

fast.en: A bright, dry day. Water is evaporating quickly from the leaves, and the whole thread of water is sliding up to replace it. Notice that the beads never bunch up or spread out. The water moves as one unbroken chain.
fast.zh: 晴朗又乾燥的一天。水從葉子上很快地蒸發，整條水柱跟著往上滑，把缺口補上。注意珠子不會擠成一堆，也不會散開：水是連成一條不斷的鏈子在移動的。

slow.en: Water is rising, but gently. Less is evaporating from the leaves, so the pull is weaker. The tree is not choosing a speed. The weather is setting it.
slow.zh: 水在上升，不過很慢。從葉子蒸發出去的水比較少，所以拉力比較弱。這不是樹在決定速度，是天氣在決定。

dark.en: It is dark. A leaf opens its pores to take in the gas it needs for making food, and that only happens in the light. So at night the pores shut, almost no water escapes, and the thread of water waits in place.
dark.zh: 天黑了。葉子打開氣孔，是為了吸進做食物要用的氣體，而那只有在有光的時候才進行。所以到了夜裡氣孔關上，幾乎沒有水散出去，水柱就停在原地等著。

humid.en: The air is already full of water vapor, so very little more can evaporate into it. The pores are open, but the pull is weak. This is also why wet clothes dry slowly on a damp day.
humid.zh: 空氣裡已經充滿水氣，所以能再蒸發進去的水很少。氣孔是開著的，可是拉力很弱。溼衣服在潮溼的日子乾得慢，也是同樣的道理。

dry.en: The soil has dried out. If the leaves kept pulling now, the thread of water could snap and let air into the tubes. So the tree shuts its pores to save water. The leaves droop, and the tree stops making food until rain comes.
dry.zh: 土乾掉了。要是葉子這時候還繼續拉，水柱可能會斷掉，讓空氣跑進管子裡。所以樹把氣孔關上，省下水分。葉子垂了下來，在下雨之前，樹也沒辦法做食物。

legend.en: Blue beads: water, moving as one chain
legend.zh: 藍色的珠子：水，連成一條鏈子在走

legend.en: Pale dots: water vapor leaving the leaves
legend.zh: 淡色的小點：離開葉子的水氣

legend.en: Green: the leaves, which turn yellowish when the tree is short of water
legend.zh: 綠色：葉子；樹缺水的時候會偏黃

legend.en: Brown: the trunk, branches, and roots, drawn see-through
legend.zh: 咖啡色：樹幹、樹枝和根，畫成透明的

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. A real trunk holds a huge number of very narrow tubes, and the model draws three thick ones. The percentages on the sliders and the speed of the water are examples. Real water in a tree moves much more slowly than the beads do. The model also leaves out the small push that roots can give from below.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的模型。真的樹幹裡有數量極多、非常細的管子；模型只畫了三條粗的。滑桿上的百分比和水的速度都是示意，真的樹裡的水走得比這些珠子慢得多。根從下面能給的那一點點推力，模型也沒有畫。
lab.credit_html: Model drawn by My Culture Connect as a teaching diagram. The ideas follow the sources listed at the bottom of this page. · 模型由人師教育協會自繪示意；原理依本頁最下方列出的出處。

paras: Stand under a tall tree and look up. Every leaf at the top needs water, and all of that water came in through the roots, far below your feet. Your heart pumps blood around your body. A tree has no heart. So how does the water get up there?

You might guess that the tree sucks it up, the way you drink through a straw. But sucking has a limit. Hundreds of years ago, people who built pumps found that suction could not raise water more than about ten meters, however hard they tried. Many trees are much taller than that.

The answer starts in the leaves. A leaf is covered with tiny pores. They open in the daytime to let in the gas the leaf needs for making food. While they are open, water inside the leaf evaporates and drifts out into the air.

Here is the important part. Water clings to itself very strongly. Inside a tree the water fills very narrow tubes, and it forms one unbroken column from the leaves all the way down to the roots. When a little water leaves at the top, it pulls the whole column up behind it, like a chain being drawn up through a pipe.

So the tree does not spend energy to lift the water. The sun and the air do the work by drying the leaves. On a bright, dry day the pull is strong. On a damp day it is weak, and at night it nearly stops.

A tree uses only a tiny part of this water to grow. Nearly all of it, from 97 to more than 99 parts in every hundred, passes straight through and out into the air. That may sound like waste, but the stream carries minerals up from the soil, and the evaporation cools the leaves.
paras_zh: 站在一棵大樹下往上看。樹頂的每一片葉子都需要水，而這些水全都是從你腳底下很深的根吸進來的。你的心臟把血液打到全身；樹沒有心臟。那麼水是怎麼上去的？
你可能會猜：樹是把水吸上去的，就像你用吸管喝飲料一樣。可是「吸」有極限。幾百年前，做抽水機的人就發現，不管怎麼努力，靠吸的最多只能把水抬高大約十公尺。很多樹比這高得多。
答案要從葉子說起。葉子上佈滿了很小的孔。這些孔在白天打開，讓葉子做食物所需要的氣體進來。孔開著的時候，葉子裡的水就蒸發，飄到空氣裡去。
接下來是關鍵。水會非常緊地黏住自己。在樹裡面，水裝在非常細的管子裡，從葉子到根連成一條不斷的水柱。上面走掉一點水，整條水柱就被往上拉，像一條鏈子從管子裡被拉上去一樣。
所以樹並沒有花力氣把水抬上去。出力的是太陽和空氣：它們把葉子弄乾。晴朗乾燥的日子，拉力很強；潮溼的日子拉力弱；到了晚上，幾乎就停了。
這些水，樹只用掉極小的一部分來生長。幾乎全部——每一百份裡有 97 份到 99 份以上——都只是穿過樹身，散到空氣裡去。聽起來很浪費，不過這股水流把礦物質從土裡帶了上來，而蒸發也讓葉子降溫。

cards.en: The pump that would not go higher
cards.zh: 再也抽不上去的抽水機
cards.body_en: People who built pumps in Italy had a problem. A suction pump could not raise water more than about ten meters, no matter how it was built. Galileo wrote about the puzzle, and his student Evangelista Torricelli solved it. The pump does not pull the water. The air outside pushes it, and the air has only so much weight. Trees, it turned out, must be doing something else.
cards.body_zh: 義大利造抽水機的人遇到一個難題：用吸的抽水機，不管怎麼造，都沒辦法把水抬高超過大約十公尺。伽利略寫下了這個謎題，他的學生托里切利解開了它：抽水機並沒有在「拉」水，是外面的空氣把水「推」上來的，而空氣的重量就只有那麼多。這麼說來，樹一定是用了別的辦法。

cards.body_en: Stephen Hales was an English clergyman who loved to measure things. In a book published in 1727 he described his experiments on plants. He compared how much water a plant took in with how much it gave off through its leaves, and his numbers showed water passing through the plant and out into the air.
cards.body_zh: 海爾斯是一位熱愛測量的英國牧師。在 1727 年出版的書裡，他記錄了自己對植物做的實驗：比較一株植物吸進多少水、又從葉子散出去多少水，他的數字顯示：水穿過植物，散到了空氣裡。

cards.en: Drops on the tips of leaves
cards.body_en: Roots can also push a little. At night, when the leaves are not pulling, the roots of some plants go on taking in water, and the pressure builds from below. By morning it forces drops of sap out at the tips or edges of the leaves. They look like dew, but they came from inside the plant. This push is much too weak to supply a tall tree.
cards.body_zh: 根也會推一點點。夜裡葉子不拉水的時候，有些植物的根還是繼續吸水，壓力從下面慢慢累積；到了早上，就把一滴一滴的汁液從葉尖或葉緣擠出來。它們看起來像露水，其實是從植物裡面出來的。這股推力太弱，供應不了一棵大樹。

cards.en: The tree that touches the sky
cards.body_en: In January 2023, a team from the Taiwan Forestry Research Institute and National Cheng Kung University walked for days into the mountains of the upper Da'an River. They had picked out one treetop from laser maps made from the air. They climbed the tree and measured it at 84.1 meters, the tallest tree known in Taiwan and in East Asia. It is a Taiwania. Because it stands out above the giants around it, the team named it the Da'an River Yitian Sword. Every drop of water at its top has been pulled up the whole way.
cards.body_zh: 2023 年 1 月，林業試驗所和成功大學組成的團隊，在大安溪上游的山區走了好幾天。他們事先從空中雷射測繪的資料裡，挑出了一個特別高的樹頂。隊員爬上那棵樹實地測量，結果是 84.1 公尺——台灣、也是東亞已知最高的樹。它是一棵台灣杉；因為它在周圍眾多巨木當中特別挺拔，團隊把它取名為「大安溪倚天劍」。它樹頂的每一滴水，都是這樣一路被拉上去的。

myths.myth_en: Trees suck water up like a straw.
myths.myth_zh: 樹像吸管一樣把水吸上去。
myths.fact_en: Suction stops at about ten meters. The water is pulled up as a column, by evaporation from the leaves.
myths.fact_zh: 用吸的只到大約十公尺。水是連成一條水柱，被葉子上的蒸發拉上去的。

myths.myth_en: The roots pump the water to the top.
myths.myth_zh: 是根把水打到樹頂的。
myths.fact_en: Roots can push only a little. Almost all of the lifting comes from the pull at the leaves.
myths.fact_zh: 根只能推一點點。幾乎所有的力氣，都來自葉子那一端的拉力。

myths.myth_en: A tree uses up all the water it drinks.
myths.myth_zh: 樹把喝進去的水都用掉了。
myths.fact_en: It keeps only a tiny part. Nearly all of the water passes through and into the air.
myths.fact_zh: 它只留下極小的一部分；幾乎所有的水都只是穿過樹身，散到空氣裡。

myths.myth_en: Water rises in a tree at the same speed all day.
myths.myth_zh: 樹裡的水整天都以同樣的速度上升。
myths.fact_en: It rises fastest on bright, dry days and nearly stops at night, when the pores are shut.
myths.fact_zh: 晴朗乾燥的時候最快；到了晚上氣孔關上，就幾乎停了。

materials.en: A clear plastic bag and a piece of string
materials.zh: 一個透明的塑膠袋和一段繩子

materials.en: A leafy branch on a living tree or bush, in the sun
materials.zh: 一根長在活的樹或灌木上、曬得到太陽、葉子多的枝條

steps.en: Slip the bag over the end of the branch so that several leaves are inside. Do not break the branch.
steps.zh: 把袋子套在枝條的末端，讓幾片葉子在袋子裡。不要把樹枝折斷。

steps.en: Tie the mouth of the bag gently around the stem.
steps.zh: 把袋口輕輕綁在枝條上。

steps.en: Look at the bag after one hour, and again after three hours. What do you see on the inside?
steps.zh: 一小時後看看袋子，三小時後再看一次。袋子裡面出現了什麼？

steps.en: Try a second bag on a branch in the shade. Which bag collects more?
steps.zh: 在陰影裡的枝條上再套一個袋子。哪一個袋子收集到的比較多？

activities.tip_en: The drops are water that came up from the roots and out through the leaves. Take the bag off on the same day, so that the leaves are not harmed.
activities.tip_zh: 那些水珠是從根上來、再從葉子散出去的水。當天就把袋子拿下來，免得傷到葉子。

materials.en: A stalk of celery with its leaves, or a white flower
materials.zh: 一根帶葉子的芹菜，或一朵白色的花

materials.en: A glass of water with food coloring in it
materials.zh: 一杯加了食用色素的水

steps.en: Ask an adult to cut the bottom off the stalk, and stand it in the colored water.
steps.zh: 請大人把芹菜的底部切掉一小段，然後把芹菜插在有顏色的水裡。

steps.en: Leave it in a bright place. Look at the leaves after a few hours, and again the next day.
steps.zh: 放在明亮的地方。幾小時後看看葉子，隔天再看一次。

steps.en: Ask the adult to cut across the stalk. Where exactly is the color?
steps.zh: 請大人把芹菜橫切開。顏色到底在哪裡？

steps.en: Set up a second stalk in a dark cupboard. Does the color travel as fast?
steps.zh: 再準備一根，放在暗的櫃子裡。顏色走得一樣快嗎？

activities.tip_en: The colored dots in the cut stalk are the tubes that carry water. Do not eat the celery afterward.
activities.tip_zh: 切面上那些有顏色的小點，就是運水的管子。做完之後這根芹菜不要吃。

sources.en: Transpiration is the movement of water through a plant and its evaporation from leaves, stems, and flowers; it is a passive process that requires no energy expense by the plant; it cools plants and carries mineral nutrients; of the water taken up, 97–99.5% is lost by transpiration and guttation; plants close their stomata to reduce water loss when uptake by the roots is less than the loss
sources.zh: 蒸散是水在植物體內移動並從葉、莖、花蒸發的過程；是被動的，植物不需耗能；能讓植物降溫並帶動礦物養分的輸送；吸收的水有 97–99.5% 經蒸散與泌溢散失；根吸水不足時植物會關閉氣孔減少失水

sources.en: The tubes of the xylem are dead at maturity and transport is passive; evaporation from the leaf cells creates a tension that pulls water up from the roots; the vessels must be very narrow or the water column would break; when the soil is dry a bubble can form and block the tube; the cohesion-tension theory was proposed in 1894 by John Joly and Henry Horatio Dixon; water transport is considered to limit the maximum height of trees
sources.zh: 木質部的管狀細胞成熟後是死細胞，輸水是被動的；葉肉細胞表面的蒸發造成張力，把水從根部拉上來；導管必須很細，否則水柱會斷；土壤乾燥時可能產生氣泡堵塞（栓塞）；內聚力—張力學說由喬利與狄克森於 1894 年提出；一般認為輸水的難度限制了樹的最大高度
